question: Which of the following is not a nitrogen mustard?

explanationHtml:
Lomustine can cross the blood-brain barrier and is used in the management of brain tumours like astrocytoma.

Nitrosoureas like lomustine and carmustine are highly lipophilic drugs and can easily cross the blood-brain barrier. Hence, they are indicated in the management of brain tumors.

Anthracycline antibiotics include doxorubicin, daunorubicin, epirubicin, valrubicin, idarubicin, and mitoxantrone.

question: Which of the following drugs is not an anthracycline antibiotic?

correctAnswer: B. A patient with laryngotracheal stenosis
explanationHtml:

Mitomycin C is an antitumor antibiotic that inhibits cell division, protein synthesis and fibroblast proliferation. Topical mitomycin C has been shown to cause symptomatic improvement when applied to patients with laryngotracheal stenosis.

question: Topical mitomycin C is used in which of the following patients?

explanationHtml:
Mitomycin C is used in the treatment of superficial transitional cell carcinoma by intravesical (into the urinary bladder) instillation.

Mitomycin C is an anti-tumor antibiotic with various uses and routes of administration:

  • Intravesical Instillation for superficial transitional cell carcinomas.
  • It is used as an IV infusion in upper gastrointestinal cancers (e.g. esophageal carcinoma), anal cancers, and breast cancers.
  • Topical mitomycin C is used in:
    • Strabismus surgery to reduce scarring
    • To prevent tracheal and esophageal stenosis
    • Post-nasal surgery synechae formation
    • During glaucoma surgery, to reduce scarring
  • Intra-ureteral for specific low-grade tumors in the ureter or renal pelvis.

Note: Cisplatin (Option C) is used for urogenital cancers, but the route of administration is intravenous.

question: A patient with superficial bladder carcinoma is being treated with a drug by intravesical therapy. Identify this drug.

explanationHtml:
Arsenic trioxide (ATO) is highly effective in relapsed or refractory acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL). It acts by enhancing reactive oxygen free radical generation in APL cells.

Tretinoin and idarubicin (anthracycline) are usually first-line agents for acute promyelocytic leukemia.
lessonTitle: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
question: A patient was diagnosed with acute promyelocytic leukemia and chemotherapy was initiated. The patient achieved complete remission. However, after a few months molecular relapse was detected. Which of the following drugs would be highly effective in this case?

explanationHtml:
Sodium 2-mercaptoethanesulfonate (MESNA) is given along with cyclophosphamide to reduce the incidence of hemorrhagic cystitis.

Hemorrhagic cystitis is a characteristic side effect of cyclophosphamide and ifosfamide. This presents as hematuria and dysuria in a patient receiving these drugs. These drugs are metabolized in the body into a toxic byproduct called acrolein. Acrolein is excreted in the urine and can severely irritate and damage the bladder lining, leading to hemorrhagic cystitis.

Hemorrhagic cystitis can be prevented by two combined strategies:

  • Sodium 2-mercaptoethanesulfonate (MESNA) directly inactivates acrolein by binding to it in the urine.
  • Vigorous hydration dilutes the concentration of acrolein in the bladder and promotes increased urine flow, which rapidly flushes acrolein from the body.

question: A 62-year-old woman with breast carcinoma is started on cyclophosphamide. What is the rationale behind using sodium 2-mercaptoethanesulfonate along with this drug?

explanationHtml:
Ifosfamide is more neurotoxic than cyclophosphamide.

Ifosfamide has the potential to cause severe neurological adverse effects, including hallucinations, coma, and death if high doses are administered. Chloroacetaldehyde (Option C) is a metabolite of ifosfamide that is responsible for these neurological adverse effects. It also causes greater platelet suppression, nephrotoxicity, and urothelial damage when compared to cyclophosphamide.

Ifosfamide is used in the treatment of osteosarcoma and testicular cancer.

Other options:

Option A: Ifosfamide is metabolized by hydroxylation by cytochrome P450 enzymes.

Option D: Ifosfamide is a nitrogen mustard (a type of alkylating agent). Cyclophosphamide, mechlorethamine, melphalan, chlorambucil, and bendamustine are also nitrogen mustards.

explanationHtml:
The patient presenting with features of heart failure and ECG changes after beginning chemotherapy depicts doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity.

Doxorubicin belongs to the anthracycline group of antitumor antibiotics, and anthracycline-induced cardiomyopathy is of two forms, depending on when symptoms appear:

  • Acute form: Presents as arrhythmias, ST and T wave changes in ECG, and reversible reduction in ejection fraction. Pericarditis-myocarditis syndrome (characterized by severe disturbances in impulse conduction and frank congestive heart failure) can also occur.
  • Chronic form: This is the more common and clinically significant form. This form is dose-dependent. It typically manifests as a progressive decline in left ventricular function, leading to dilated cardiomyopathy and potentially irreversible heart failure

Doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity is irreversible and dose-dependent. In contrast, trastuzumab-induced cardiotoxicity is typically reversible and not dose-dependent.

Note: Dexrazoxane is a cardioprotective iron-chelating agent that is indicated for use along with high-dose doxorubicin to prevent cardiotoxicity. The exact cardioprotective mechanism of dexrazoxane is unknown, and it appears not to compromise with anticancer activity of doxorubicin.

question: A 67 year old woman with a malignant lump in the breast who is undergoing chemotherapy, presents with shortness of breath, tachycardia and hypertension. ECG shows ST and T wave changes. Which among the following drugs could have led to this?

explanationHtml:
Doxorubicin requires dose adjustment during or after radiotherapy in order to prevent radiation toxicity.

Anthracyclines like doxorubicin can result in a radiation recall reaction, where erythema and desquamation of skin are observed at sites of previous radiation therapy. The risk of cardiotoxicity also increases with previous irradiation. Therefore, careful monitoring and dosage adjustments are required for doxorubicin.

question: While reviewing the drug chart of a patient undergoing radiotherapy, which of the following drugs would require a dose adjustment to prevent radiation toxicity?

explanationHtml:
Sustained neutropenia is seen with nitrosoureas.

Nitrosoureas (carmustine and lomustine) are known to cause severe myelosuppression which is slow in onset and can take 4 to 6 weeks to recover from after just one treatment dose.

Other chemotherapeutic agents also commonly cause neutropenia, but the recovery is faster than that of nitrosoureas.
lessonTitle: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
question: A patient is undergoing chemotherapy for glioblastoma multiforme. You notice that his serial blood investigations reveal sustained neutropenia. Which of the following drugs could have caused this?

explanationHtml:
In the given clinical scenario, the patient develops symptoms like restlessness and flushing upon taking alcohol after his medication, which is suggestive of a disulfiram-like reaction. This is a known adverse effect of the alkylating agent, procarbazine. Procarbazine is also associated with behavioural disturbances and sedation.

Some important drugs that cause a disulfiram-like reaction are:

  • Procarbazine
  • Metronidazole, Tinidazole
  • Some cephalosporins, like cefoperazone, cefotetan
  • 1st generation sulfonylureas like tolbutamide, chlorpropamide

These drugs inhibit aldehyde dehydrogenase, similar to disulfiram. When alcohol is combined with these drugs, acetaldehyde accumulates in the body and causes unpleasant symptoms like flushing, sweating, tachycardia, hypotension, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, and headache.

Procarbazine is also a weak MAO inhibitor and can therefore cause hypertension in patients exposed to foods containing high amounts of tyramine like aged cheeses, cured meats and wine.
lessonTitle: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
question: A patient with Hodgkin’s disease on chemotherapy with an alkylating agent develops behavioral disturbances and experiences sedation. He also complains of severe restlessness, palpitations, facial flushing, and sweating whenever he takes alcohol after taking this alkylating agent. What is the drug being described here?

explanationHtml:
The progression of neuropathy even after cessation depicts the coasting phenomenon, which is seen with cisplatin.

Neurotoxicity is usually dependent on the cumulative dose of anticancer drugs. The severity of neuropathy increases with the duration of treatment, and progression stops once drug treatment is completed. Platinum compounds like cisplatin and oxaliplatin are an exception, where sensory loss progresses for several months after cessation of treatment. This event is known as coasting.
lessonTitle: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
question: A 50 year old man who presented with dysphagia was diagnosed with esophageal carcinoma and underwent multiple cycles of chemotherapy. During the cycles, he had developed tingling and numbness in the lower limbs and the symptoms progressed even after cessation of the cycles. Which drug could have led to this?

explanationHtml:
The scenario is suggestive of secondary leukemia, which is associated with cisplatin (and other platinum compounds) and alkylating agents.

Secondary leukemia arises when these agents damage the DNA of healthy bone marrow cells, leading to new genetic mutations that cause these cells to become cancerous. Cisplatin is associated with the development of AML, usually more than 4 years after treatment. Cisplatin produces responses in cancers of the bladder, head and neck, cervix, and endometrium; all forms of carcinoma of the lung; anal and rectal carcinomas; and neoplasms of childhood.

Note: Procarbazine, a monofunctional alkylating agent, is most commonly associated with the development of secondary leukemias.
lessonTitle: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
question: A 65 year old man who was diagnosed with small cell carcinoma of the lung had undergone chemotherapy about 5 years ago. Now he presents with features suggestive of acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Which of the following drugs could have caused this condition?

explanationHtml:
The given scenario is suggestive of nephrotoxicity, and it is one of the limiting adverse effects of cisplatin therapy.

The kidneys are the primary route for cisplatin excretion. Cisplatin actively accumulates in the proximal renal tubules. This accumulation leads to direct damage to tubular cells and indirect damage by inflammation, ultimately leading to cellular necrosis. The resulting injury can present as acute kidney injury and electrolyte imbalances. A high concentration of chloride stabilizes cisplatin and reduces nephrotoxicity. Therefore, chloride diuresis is used to reduce nephrotoxicity. Amifostine and mannitol are also used to reduce cisplatin-induced nephrotoxicity.

Other options:

Option B: Streptozotocin use can result in diabetes mellitus due to the destruction of beta cells of the pancreas.

Option C: Methysergide use is associated with retroperitoneal fibrosis.

Option D: Cyclophosphamide causes hemorrhagic cystitis as one of its characteristic side effects.
lessonTitle: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
question: A patient who was diagnosed with gastric carcinoma is undergoing chemotherapy. His serum creatinine levels are rising and you suspect renal tubular damage caused by one of his chemotherapeutic drugs. Which drug could it be?

explanationHtml:
Cisplatin is a highly emetogenic anticancer drug. Cisplatin causes marked nausea and vomiting in almost all cases and is usually administered along with anti-emetic regimens.

Cisplatin-induced nausea and vomiting can usually be controlled with 5HT3 receptor antagonists, neurokinin (NK1) receptor antagonists (e.g., aprepitant), and high-dose corticosteroids.
lessonTitle: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
question: Which among the following is a highly emetogenic anticancer drug?

explanationHtml:
Pulmonary fibrosis is commonly seen with bleomycin.

Bleomycin leads to the destruction of both type I and type II pneumocytes. Instead of regeneration, which is the normal function of type II pneumocytes, the damaged type II cells release pro-fibrotic mediators, thereby actively contributing to the excessive collagen deposition and scarring that characterizes pulmonary fibrosis.

Pulmonary toxicity begins with a dry cough, fine rales, and diffuse basal infiltrates on X-ray and may progress to life-threatening pulmonary fibrosis. No specific treatment is available to ameliorate the toxicity, and is managed by general symptomatic care.

Note: A few case reports of methotrexate causing pulmonary fibrosis have been reported. The association is still uncertain as the underlying disease process, like rheumatoid arthritis(RA), can also contribute to fibrosis. Methotrexate causes pneumonitis and is not proven to cause pulmonary fibrosis.
lessonTitle: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
question: A patient who is undergoing chemotherapy for testicular cancer, now presents with dyspnea and dry cough. Investigations suggest pulmonary fibrosis. This condition is commonly  associated with which of the following drugs?

explanationHtml:
Sinusoidal obstruction syndrome is most commonly associated with high-dose busulfan. Incidence increases when coadministered with CYP inhibitors.

Sinusoidal obstruction syndrome, previously known as veno-occlusive hepatic disease (VOD), involves primary hepatic sinusoidal injury that progresses to diffuse hepatocyte involvement and panvasculitis. This leads to multi-organ failure and can be life-threatening.

Other chemotherapeutic agents, like cyclophosphamide, are also known to cause sinusoidal obstruction syndrome, but busulfan is most commonly associated.
lessonTitle: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
question: A patient who is undergoing chemotherapy, now presents with weight gain, ascites, hepatomegaly and hyperbilirubinemia. You suspect sinusoidal obstruction syndrome. Which drug is the most common cause of this condition?

explanationHtml:
L-asparaginase causes a hypercoagulable state as an adverse effect.

The toxicity of L-asparaginase arises due to inhibition of protein synthesis in normal tissues, examples of which are given below:

  • Thrombosis and increased coagulation occur as the synthesis of physiological anticoagulation factors is impaired.
  • Hemorrhage and bleeding occur as the synthesis of clotting factors is impaired.
  • Hyperglycemia occurs as the synthesis of insulin is impaired.
  • Hypertriglyceridemia occurs as the synthesis of lipoproteins is impaired.
lessonTitle: Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
question: A patient undergoing chemotherapy was brought to the ER with seizures. He is diagnosed with cerebrovascular accident which you suspect to be due to a drug-induced hypercoagulable state. Which of the following drugs is implicated?

explanationHtml:
Bleomycin causes a unique side effect called flagellate hyperpigmentation or flagellate erythema, which presents as band-like linear streaks. The appearance of these manifestations can range from red (erythematous) to darkening (hyperpigmented) and commonly affects the arms, back, scalp, and hands. Topical corticosteroids typically help improve the symptoms.

The image below shows a classical example of flagellate hyperpigmentation.

question: Which of the following drugs causes flagellate pigmentation?

explanationHtml:
The only chemotherapeutic agent that has been proven to cause bladder cancer is cyclophosphamide.

The risk of the bladder cancer formation is linearly related to the duration and intensity of cyclophosphamide treatment, supporting a causative role. Phosphoramide mustard is the primary mutagenic metabolite that causes bladder cancer in patients exposed to cyclophosphamide.

correctAnswer: A. Palliation in head and neck cancer
explanationHtml:
Cetuximab is used for palliation in head and neck cancer.

Indications for use of cetuximab are:

  • Advanced squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck in combination with radiotherapy for locally or regionally
  • Metastatic colorectal cancer

Cetuximab is a recombinant chimeric monoclonal antibody against the external domain of the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR).

question: Cetuximab is approved for use in which of the following conditions?

question: A patient diagnosed with metastatic colorectal carcinoma is being treated with panitumumab. This drug acts against which of the following receptors?

Trastuzumab is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody that targets HER2, blocking its signaling and inducing immune-mediated cytotoxicity.

Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 tyrosine kinase receptor (HER-2-TK) inhibitors are:

Anti-Her-2 monoclonal antibodies are:

question: A 57-year-old woman is diagnosed with HER 2/neu positive breast cancer. Which of the following monoclonal antibodies is indicated for the management of this patient?

explanationHtml:

It is indicated in the management of adjuvant therapy in early and metastatic HER-2 positive breast cancer.

question: A 57-year-old woman diagnosed with breast carcinoma was prescribed trastuzumab. Which of the following statements regarding this drug is true?

explanationHtml:
The most serious toxicity of trastuzumab is cardiac failure. Cardiac failure is a potentially disabling or fatal side effect unless recognized early and the drug is discontinued.

Cardiotoxicity is caused by the interruption of HER2/4 heterodimer signaling in cardiomyocytes, which is a type of signaling that is essential for the maintenance of contractile function.

Clinical correlation:

  • Baseline ECG and cardiac ejection fraction should be monitored to rule out underlying heart disease
  • Careful clinical follow-up for signs and symptoms of CHF

Other side effects include fever, chills, nausea, dyspnea, and rashes. Dose-limiting toxicities are side effects of a drug or other treatment that are serious enough to prevent an increase in dose or level of that treatment.

Note: Cardiotoxicity of antineoplastic agents

Mechanism Type 1 cardiotoxicity, due to necrosis due to reactive oxygen species Type 2 cardiotoxicity, due to HER2 signaling block in myocardial cells

question: A patient was diagnosed with HER2/neu positive breast cancer and was started on adjuvant therapy with trastuzumab. Which of the following is the most serious and dose-limiting toxicity of this drug?

explanationHtml:
Ranibizumab is associated with a raise in IOP, not a fall.

Ranibizumab is a monoclonal antibody directed against VEGF-A (vascular endothelial growth factor-A). Ranibizumab is indicated in wet age-related macular degeneration and is used intravitreally where it inhibits VEGF-A induced ocular neovascularization.

[[figure-1]]
question: All of the following are known side effects of intravitreal ranibizumab, except _______.

explanationHtml:
Ramucirumab is a monoclonal antibody that binds to VEGFR-2 and inhibits the binding of VEGFR ligands.

It is indicated in NSCLC, gastric cancer and metastatic colorectal cancer.

Bevacizumab, aflibercept, and ranibizumab are monoclonal antibodies against VEGF ligands and not the receptor.
question: Which among the following is the monoclonal antibody that is targeted specifically against VEGFR?

explanationHtml:
Rituximab is used in all conditions, except paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria.

Indications for rituximab include: (mnemonic- CANT MIS Ritu):

  • CLL
  • Autoimmune hemolytic anemia
  • Non-Hodgkin lymphoma
  • TTP
  • Marginal zone lymphomas, mantle cell lymphoma, myasthenia gravis
  • ITP
  • SLE
  • Rheumatoid arthritis

It is a chimeric monoclonal antibody targeted against the CD20 receptor that is present on the surface of B lymphocytes.

Ofatumumab and obinutuzumab are the other monoclonal antibodies directed against CD20 receptors. They are also approved for use in CLL.
question: Rituximab is not used in which of the following conditions?

explanationHtml:
Alemtuzumab is a humanized monoclonal antibody against CD52 that is indicated in the management of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL).

Alemtuzumab binds to CD52, a surface antigen present on mature lymphocytes (T and B cells) and some monocytes/macrophages. This causes antibody-dependent cell-mediated lysis (ADCC) and complement-mediated destruction of these immune cells.

Rituximab and obinutuzumab are monoclonal antibodies against CD20 that are also indicated in the treatment of chronic lymphocytic leukemia. (Option A and D)

Cetuximab is a chimeric human-mouse anti-epidermal growth factor receptor monoclonal antibody against the extracellular domain of EGFR. (Option C)
question: A 70-year-old man is found to have leukocytosis on his yearly health check-up.  Further evaluation led to a diagnosis of chronic lymphocytic leukemia. Immunophenotyping was positive for CD52. Which is the monoclonal antibody indicated in this condition?

explanationHtml:
Pertuzumab is a monoclonal antibody against the HER2 receptor.

Pertuzumab is indicated in HER2-positive breast cancer in combination with trastuzumab and docetaxel.

Monoclonal antibodies against EGFR (HER1) are:

  • Panitumumab
  • Cetuximab
  • Necitumumab
question: Which of the following monoclonal antibodies is not a HER1 inhibitor?

explanationHtml:
Olaratumab is a monoclonal antibody against PDGFR-alpha and blocks ligand-mediated receptor activation. It is indicated along with doxorubicin for adult patients with soft tissue sarcoma.

Panitumumab and cetuximab are monoclonal antibodies against EGFR (HER1).

Pertuzumab is a monoclonal antibody against HER2.
question: Which of the following is a monoclonal antibody directed against PDGFR-alpha?

explanationHtml:
Blinatumomab is a bispecific monoclonal antibody.

A bispecific monoclonal antibody simultaneously binds to two different types of antigen. It binds simultaneously to CD3 on T cells and to CD19 on B cells. This links the two cells and activates T cells to exert cytotoxic activity against CD19 B cells. Blinatumomab is approved for the treatment of Philadelphia chromosome-negative relapsed or refractory B-cell precursor ALL.

Other options:

Option A: Daratumumab is a monoclonal antibody against CD-38.

Option B: Alemtuzumab is a monoclonal antibody against CD-52.

Option D: Panitumumab is a monoclonal antibody against EGFR.
question: Which of the following is a bispecific monoclonal antibody?

explanationHtml:
Ibritumomab tiuxetan is a radioimmunoconjugate that is approved for use in non-Hodgkin's lymphoma. Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma is a subtype of non-Hodgkin lymphoma.

Ibritumomab is a monoclonal antibody against CD20, which is attached to the radioactive isotope yttrium-90 using the chelator tiuxetan. Beta emission from Y-90 destroys the surrounding tissues.

Radioimmunoconjugates provide targeted delivery of radionuclides to tumor cells. It is made by attaching a radioactive molecule to a monoclonal antibody.

Other options:

Option A: Gemtuzumab ozogamicin is a monoclonal antibody against CD33 covalently linked to a semisynthetic derivative of calicheamicin which is a potent antitumor antibiotic.

Option B: Brentuximab vedotin is a monoclonal antibody against CD30 linked with a microtubule-disrupting agent, MMAE.

Option C: Denileukin diftitox is an immunotoxin produced by the genetic recombination of IL-2 and the catalytically active fragment of diphtheria toxin.
question: A 40-year-old man who presented with fever, night sweats and weight loss was evaluated and diagnosed with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. Which of the following is a radioimmunoconjugate that can be used in this condition?

explanationHtml:
Basiliximab exhibits a high affinity towards IL-2 receptor and inhibits it.
Basiliximab is an anti-CD-25 monoclonal antibody. It has a short plasma half-life of 1 week. It is used to prevent transplant rejection reactions. Its adverse effects are anaphylactic reactions & opportunistic infections.
question: What is basiliximab?

explanationHtml:
The patient presented with a palpable abdominal mass and elevated levels of urinary homovanillic acid and vanillyl mandelic acid. The histopathology image shows small round blue tumor cells with Homer-Wright pseudorosettes, which point towards a diagnosis of paediatric neuroblastoma. Dinutuximab is a monoclonal antibody against glycolipid GD2, which is indicated in this condition.

GD2 glycolipid is expressed on the following cells:

  • Neuroblastoma cells
  • Normal cells of neuroectodermal origin, central nervous system, peripheral nerves.

[[figure-1]]
question: A 2-year-old girl was brought with complaints of abdominal pain and diarrhea. Examination revealed a palpable abdominal mass. Investigations showed elevated levels of urinary homovanillic acid and vanillyl mandelic acid. The lesion could not be completely resected during surgery, and histopathology findings are shown in the image. Which of the following is a monoclonal antibody approved for use in this condition?

explanationHtml:
Pembrolizumab is the drug recently approved for the treatment of colorectal cancer arising through Lynch syndrome. The increased risk for colorectal cancer in Lynch Syndrome is due to inherited mutations that impair DNA mismatch repair.

Immune checkpoint inhibitors inhibit proteins that help to keep immune responses to cancer cells in check. When these proteins are blocked, the brake on the immune system is released and T cells are able to kill cancer cells more efficiently.

Pembrolizumab is an immune checkpoint inhibitor. It is a humanized monoclonal IgG4-κ isotype antibody that blocks the interaction between programmed cell death protein (PD-1) and its ligands.

The FDA has approved pembrolizumab for patients with recurrent, locally advanced or metastatic, squamous cell carcinoma of the esophagus and head and neck squamous cell cancer in combination with platin agents and 5-FU for the first-line treatment.
question: Which of the following drugs is recently approved for the treatment of colorectal cancer arising through Lynch Syndrome?

explanationHtml:
Pembrolizumab is not approved for use in small-cell lung cancer.

Pembrolizumab is a monoclonal antibody (IgG4) against PD-1 and blocks interaction between PD-1 and its ligands PD-L1 and PD-L2. It is used in the following conditions:

  • Hodgkin’s lymphoma
  • Metastatic urothelial cancer
  • Metastatic non-SCLC
  • Merkel cell carcinoma
  • Chemotherapy-refractory head and neck cancers
  • Refractory melanoma
  • Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
  • Esophageal Cancer
  • Colorectal cancer due to Lynch syndrome

Note: Pembrolizumab was indicated for metastatic SCLC, but this indication has recently been discontinued by the FDA.
question: Pembrolizumab is not approved for use in which of the following malignancies?

explanationHtml:
Reslizumab is a monoclonal antibody against interleukin-5 that is approved for use in severe asthma.

Interleukin-5 plays an important role in eosinophilic inflammation and is also involved in eosinophil survival through activation of the specific receptor, IL-5Rα, on eosinophils. Anti–IL–5 and anti–IL–5 receptor (IL-5Rα) blocking antibodies inhibit eosinophilic inflammation in asthmatic patients. Three antibodies are approved for use in severe eosinophilic asthma. The anti–IL–5 antibodies mepolizumab and reslizumab block circulating IL-5. Benralizumab blocks IL-5Rα.

Other options:

Options A & B: Omalizumab is an anti-IgE antibody, and lebrikizumab is an antibody against interleukin 13, which are also indicated in the management of asthma.

Option D: Atezolizumab is an immune checkpoint modulator that inhibits the interaction of PD-L1 with PD-1 and B7-H1. It is approved for use in metastatic urothelial cancer and NSCLC.
question: Which among the following is an interleukin-5 antagonist indicated in the management of asthma?

explanationHtml:
Obiltoxaximab is a monoclonal antibody against the protective antigen of Bacillus anthracis.

It is indicated in the treatment of inhalational anthrax due to B. anthracis in combination with appropriate antibacterial drugs. It is also indicated for prophylaxis of inhalational anthrax.
question: Which of the following is the monoclonal antibody developed against Bacillus anthracis?

explanationHtml:
Durvalumab is an immune checkpoint inhibitor. It is an antagonist of PD-L1, which is a protein-ligand that is present on antigen-presenting cells, T cells, B cells, and some cancer cells.

Immune checkpoint inhibitors inhibit proteins that help the cancer cells evade the immune response. When these proteins are blocked, the brake on the immune system is released, and T cells are able to kill cancer cells more efficiently.

Durvalumab is approved for use in metastatic urothelial cancer. The FDA approved durvalumab in combination with etoposide and either carboplatin or cisplatin as first-line treatment of patients with extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer.

Other PD-L1 inhibitors include atezolizumab and avelumab.
question: Which of the following is an immune checkpoint inhibitor?

explanationHtml:
Baricitinib is a Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor approved for use in the treatment of adult patients with moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis who have had an inadequate response to one or more tumor necrosis factor (TNF) blockers.

Oral Janus kinase inhibitors indicated for rheumatoid arthritis are baricitinib and tofacitinib

Other options:

Option A: Ruxolitinib is a Janus kinase inhibitor approved for use in various forms of myelofibrosis, polycythemia vera, and acute and chronic graft vs host disease. It is not indicated for rheumatoid arthritis.

Options C and D: Dasatinib and ponatinib are BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase inhibitors indicated for CML.
question: A patient with severe rheumatoid arthritis has inadequate disease control with infliximab. Which Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor can you add to his treatment regimen?

explanationHtml:
The scenario described in the question points towards a diagnosis of chronic plaque psoriasis. Tildrakizumab is a monoclonal antibody directed against IL-23 used in the treatment of this condition.

IL-23 is a naturally occurring cytokine that is involved in inflammatory and immune responses. Tildrakizumab prevents the interaction of IL-23 with its receptors. It is indicated in moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis.

Secukinumab, ixekizumab, and brodalumab are monoclonal antibodies directed against IL-17A and are also indicated in moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis.

Note: Ustekinumab is a monoclonal antibody against both IL-12 and IL-23. It is used to treat Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, plaque psoriasis, and psoriatic arthritis.
question: A patient has presented to the OPD with raised erythematous plaques on his arms and torso covered in silvery scales. You decide to prescribe a monoclonal antibody targeting interleukin-23 for treatment. Identify this drug.

explanationHtml:
Dupilumab is indicated in the treatment of moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis, when topical therapies are not effective.

Dupilumab is a monoclonal antibody against the receptor IL-4Rα. Both IL-4 and IL-13 use this receptor for signalling. When the action of these interleukins is inhibited, it results in a decrease in the immune response, including the release of proinflammatory cytokines, chemokines, and IgE. It is also indicated for moderate-severe asthma and inadequately controlled chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps.
question: Dupilumab is indicated in the management of _______.

correctAnswer: C. Blocks the action of BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase
explanationHtml:
Imatinib mesylate blocks the action of the chimeric fusion protein of BCR-ABL. It targets the BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase and inhibits its activity.

The Philadelphia chromosome translocation t(9;22) leads to expression of ABL and BCR. This fusion generates a constitutively active tyrosine kinase, BCR-ABL, resulting in continuous and uncontrollable cell division. BCR-ABL drives the malignant phenotype of chronic myelocytic leukemia (CML). Imatinib causes remission in >90% of patients in the chronic phase of CML.

The same mechanism of imatinib also explains its use in Philadelphia-positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL).
lessonTitle: Interleukins, Growth Factors And Targeted Therapies

options.text: Blocking the action of P glycoprotein
Blocks the action of BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase
Blocks the action of PD-1 receptors

question: What is the mechanism of action of imatinib mesylate?

explanationHtml:
Erlotinib is an epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) inhibitor.

Classification of BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase inhibitors:

  • First-generation: most likely to develop resistance.
    • Imatinib
  • Second generation: active against imatinib-resistant CML cases but not against T315I mutant cases.
    • Nilotinib
    • Dasatinib
    • Bosutinib
  • Third generation: active against T315I mutant CML cases and other known mutant cases.
    • Ponatinib
lessonTitle: Interleukins, Growth Factors And Targeted Therapies
question: Which of the following is not a BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase inhibitor?

explanationHtml:
The drug of choice for the management of a patient with a c-KIT positive metastatic gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) is imatinib.

It is an oral anticancer drug that acts by inhibiting tyrosine kinase activated due to BCR-ABL fusion. It also inhibits other related tyrosine kinases and hence is used in the treatment of conditions like gastrointestinal stromal tumor (driven by a c-KIT mutation).

Imatinib is the agent of choice for GIST patients with unresectable and/or metastatic disease and as adjuvant therapy following surgery of c-kit positive GIST.
lessonTitle: Interleukins, Growth Factors And Targeted Therapies
question: A patient presented with abdominal pain. Imaging revealed a mass in the small intestine and a lesion in the liver. A diagnosis of a c-KIT positive gastrointestinal stromal tumor with liver metastasis was made on further evaluation. What is the drug of choice?

correctAnswer: C. Point mutations in kinase domain
explanationHtml:
The given scenario is suggestive of the development of resistance to imatinib, which is a tyrosine kinase inhibitor. This condition arises due to point mutations in three separate regions of the kinase domain.

The contact points between imatinib and the tyrosine kinase become sites of mutations in drug-resistant leukemic cells, and hence these mutations prevent tight binding of the drug and lock the enzyme in its open configuration (the configuration in which it has access to the substrate and is enzymatically active).

Mechanisms other than BCR-ABL kinase mutations play a minor role in resistance to imatinib. They include:

  • Amplification of the wild-type kinase gene has been identified in some cases (Option A)
  • Overexpression of the MDR gene, leading to increased drug efflux transporter, has been shown experimentally but not implicated in clinical resistance. (Option B & D)

Nilotinib retains inhibitory activity in the presence of most point mutations that confer resistance to imatinib.
lessonTitle: Interleukins, Growth Factors And Targeted Therapies
question: A patient with chronic myeloid leukemia was switched to nilotinib as he showed only a partial response to imatinib therapy. What is the most likely mechanism resulting in the loss of response?

explanationHtml:
Imatinib is the agent of choice in patients with unresectable and/or metastatic GIST and as adjuvant therapy for c-kit positive GIST. Imatinib also shows therapeutic benefits in patients with hypereosinophilia syndrome and dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans (driven by activating mutations in the PDGFR).

Imatinib is an oral anticancer drug that acts by inhibiting tyrosine kinase activated due to ABL-BCR fusion. Imatinib also inhibits other kinases and hence is used in the above-mentioned conditions.

Indications for imatinib are:

  • BCR-ABL kinase mutations:
    • Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML)
    • Acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL)
  • C-KIT mutations -gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST)
  • PDGFR mutations:
    • Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
    • Hypereosinophilia syndrome
    • Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML)
lessonTitle: Interleukins, Growth Factors And Targeted Therapies
question:
Imatinib is indicated in which of the following patients?

  1. 53-year-old with gastrointestinal stromal tumor
  2. 43-year-old with pyoderma gangrenosum
  3. 38-year-old with dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
  4. 60-year-old with autoimmune hepatitis
  5. 35-year-old with hypereosinophilia syndrome

explanationHtml:
Ponatinib is a third-generation BCR-ABL kinase inhibitor.

Classification of BCR-ABL kinase inhibitors:

  • First-generation: most likely to develop resitance.
    • Imatinib
  • Second-generation: active against imatinib-resistant CML cases but not against T315I mutant cases.
    • Nilotinib
    • Dasatinib
    • Bosutinib
  • Third-generation: active against T315I mutant CML cases and other known mutant cases.
    • Ponatinib
lessonTitle: Interleukins, Growth Factors And Targeted Therapies
question: Which of the following is a third generation BCR-ABL kinase inhibitor?

correctAnswer: D. Dual inhibitor of EGFR and HER 2 tyrosine kinase
explanationHtml:
Lapatinib is a dual inhibitor of epidermal growth factor (EGFR) and human epidermal growth factor 2 (HER2) tyrosine kinase.

Lapatinib in combination with capecitabine is approved for the treatment of patients with metastatic HER2-positive trastuzumab-refractory breast cancer.
lessonTitle: Interleukins, Growth Factors And Targeted Therapies

options.text: Dual inhibitor of VEGFR and HER 2 tyrosine kinase
Dual inhibitor of MET and HER 2 tyrosine kinase
Dual inhibitor of VEGFR and MET tyrosine kinase
Dual inhibitor of EGFR and HER 2 tyrosine kinase

question: A patient with trastuzumab-refractory breast cancer is started on lapatinib. Which of the following statements is true regarding this drug?

explanationHtml:
Afatinib binds covalently with epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase (EGFR-TK), also known as HER-1 receptor, and inhibits it irreversibly. It is approved for use in metastatic non-small cell lung cancer with EGFR mutations.

Gefitinib and erlotinib compete with ATP binding to EGFR and result in competitive inhibition, which is reversible.
lessonTitle: Interleukins, Growth Factors And Targeted Therapies
question: Which among the following is an irreversible inhibitor of EGFR tyrosine kinase?

explanationHtml:
Hypertension is one of the characteristic side effects of angiogenesis inhibitors like bevacizumab.

The mechanism of hypertension is not clear but may be related to decreased endothelial nitric oxide production. Patients receiving higher doses and prolonged treatment might require antihypertensive medications. Other side effects of bevacizumab include gastrointestinal perforation, thromboembolic events, hemorrhage, proteinuria, and wound-healing complications.

Bevacizumab can be used in the treatment of metastatic colon cancer, in combination with the FOLFOX or FOLFIRI regimen. It can also be used in the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer.
lessonTitle: Interleukins, Growth Factors And Targeted Therapies
question: A patient undergoing treatment for colon cancer develops hypertension. Which of the following drugs is most commonly implicated?

explanationHtml:
Aflibercept is more efficacious than bevacizumab or ranibizumab in patients with poor baseline values of visual impairment with diabetic macular edema.

Aflibercept, bevacizumab, and ranibizumab are all anti-VEGF (vascular endothelial growth factor) agents used to treat diabetic macular edema (DME) by targeting VEGF, a key protein that causes leaky blood vessels and fluid buildup in the macula. All of them are administered intravitreally. Clinical trials have shown the advantage of aflibercept over bevacizumab and ranibizumab in visual and anatomic terms at the end of one year.

Ramucirumab, which is a monoclonal antibody against VEGFR, is not indicated for diabetic macular edema.
lessonTitle: Interleukins, Growth Factors And Targeted Therapies
question: A patient with uncontrolled diabetes is diagnosed with diabetic macular edema. Which of the following anti-VEGF therapies is most effective in the treatment of this condition?

explanationHtml:
Sorafenib is indicated as a first-line treatment for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma. It is an angiogenesis inhibitor.

Hepatocellular carcinoma management:

  • Resection, ablation, and other physical measures are the mainstay.
  • Only two drugs (angiogenesis inhibitors) are approved in this condition:
    • Sorafenib (first-line)
    • Regorafenib (second-line).

Sunitinib and thalidomide are not indicated in hepatocellular carcinoma.
lessonTitle: Interleukins, Growth Factors And Targeted Therapies
question: A patient is referred to your center for the management of hepatocellular carcinoma. Imaging reveals a large lesion in the liver with multiple intrahepatic metastases. The tumor is found to be unresectable. Which of the following is considered as first-line treatment for this patient?

explanationHtml:
Thalidomide use is associated with an adverse effect of peripheral neuropathy and is usually avoided in HIV-associated peripheral neuropathy, as it can worsen the condition.

It is being investigated as an orphan drug for:

  • Recurrent aphthous ulcers
  • Graft vs host disease (GVHD)
  • Behcet syndrome
  • Primary brain malignancies
  • Kaposi's sarcoma
  • Crohn’s disease.

It is FDA-approved for use in multiple myeloma and erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL).

Note: In utero exposure can cause limb abnormalities (phocomelia), as well as other congenital anomalies. Thalidomide should never be taken by women who are pregnant or who could become pregnant while taking the drug. It may also cause an irreversible neuropathy.
lessonTitle: Interleukins, Growth Factors And Targeted Therapies
question: Thalidomide should not be used in which of the following conditions?

explanationHtml:
Lenalidomide, which is a congener of thalidomide, suppresses bone marrow and is associated with significant leukopenia.

Lenalidomide carries the black box warning for hematological toxicity since it can cause significant neutropenia and thrombocytopenia. Its use is associated with a lesser incidence of sedation, constipation, and neuropathy when compared to thalidomide.

Note: Thalidomide and lenalidomide increase the risk of thromboembolic events, including deep vein thrombosis, stroke, and myocardial infarction. This is also a black box warning for both drugs.
lessonTitle: Interleukins, Growth Factors And Targeted Therapies
question: Use of lenalidomide over thalidomide would lead to the reduction of incidence of the following side effects, except ___________.

explanationHtml:
Bortezomib is a proteasome inhibitor.

The primary function of the proteasome is to degrade proteins that have been tagged for destruction with ubiquitin. This tagging process is important for identifying proteins that are misfolded, damaged, or no longer needed. Bortezomib binds to the proteasome and inhibits its proteolytic activity, which leads to an accumulation of toxic proteins, causing cellular stress and ultimately triggering apoptosis. It is indicated in the management of multiple myeloma.

Other options:

Option A: Paclitaxel is a taxane. It stabilises microtubules.

Option C: Cetuximab is a monoclonal antibody against the extracellular domain of EGFR.

Option D: Irinotecan is a topoisomerase I inhibitor.
lessonTitle: Interleukins, Growth Factors And Targeted Therapies
question: Which of the following is a proteasome inhibitor?

explanationHtml:
Tamoxifen is a selective estrogen receptor modulator that is indicated for hormone-responsive breast cancer.

Tamoxifen is approved for endocrine treatment of women with estrogen receptor-positive (ER+) metastatic breast cancer or adjuvant therapy of adult patients with early-stage ER+ breast cancer. It is also used to reduce the incidence of breast cancer in adult women at high risk.

Tamoxifen is associated with serious adverse effects like uterine malignancies, stroke, and pulmonary embolism.
lessonTitle: Interleukins, Growth Factors And Targeted Therapies
question: Which of the following drugs can be used for the treatment of a patient with hormone-responsive breast cancer?

explanationHtml:
Amifostine is the radioprotective drug that has been prescribed to this patient.

It is an organic thiophosphate cytoprotective agent that is indicated for the following conditions:

  • Reduction of xerostomia in patients with head and neck cancer undergoing postoperative irradiation where the radiation port includes a substantial portion of the parotid glands.
  • Reduction of nephrotoxicity associated with cisplatin.
lessonTitle: Interleukins, Growth Factors And Targeted Therapies
question: A patient undergoing adjuvant radiotherapy for an oral malignancy is prescribed a radioprotective drug. Identify this drug.

explanationHtml:
Palbociclib is a cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) 4/6 inhibitor.

CDK4/6 are proteins that drive cancer cells to grow and divide by allowing them to progress through the cell cycle (specifically, from the G1 to the S phase). Palbociclib blocks these proteins, thereby preventing cancer cells from dividing uncontrollably. It is approved for use in advanced or metastatic ER-positive HER2-negative breast cancer.

Other options:

Option A: Ruxolitinib is an inhibitor of Janus associated kinases (JAK1 and JAK2).

Options C & D: Trametinib and cobimetinib are inhibitors of serine-threonine kinases.
lessonTitle: Interleukins, Growth Factors And Targeted Therapies
question: Which among the following is a cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) 4/6 inhibitor?

explanationHtml:
Vemurafenib and dabrafenib inhibit the V600E mutated BRAF present in melanoma.

BRAF mutations confer constitutive activation of the kinase pathway independent of RAS activation. BRAF is mutated in more than half of the melanomas, and 90% of these mutations display a substitution of valine to glutamic acid (V600E) or to lysine (V600K), which results in constitutive protein kinase activation. Vemurafenib and dabrafenib are inhibitors of mutated BRAF and are indicated in the management of melanoma. The name vemurafenib is derived from the target V600E mutated BRAF.

Ibrutinib (Option D) is a Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitor.
lessonTitle: Interleukins, Growth Factors And Targeted Therapies
question: Which of the following inhibits the V600E mutated BRAF, a mutation commonly found in melanoma?

explanationHtml:
Vismodegib acts as a competitive antagonist of the SMO (smoothens hedgehog) receptor in the hedgehog signaling pathway.

Hedgehog signaling plays a key role in stem cell regulation and tissue regeneration. Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) is associated with dysregulation of this pathway. Vismodegib is indicated in patients with metastatic or relapsed BCC.

Other options:

Option A: Vemurafenib is a BRAF kinase inhibitor.

Option C: Olaparib is an inhibitor of PARP [Poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase] enzyme.

Option D: Neratinib is an irreversible inhibitor of HER-2 and EGFR.
lessonTitle: Interleukins, Growth Factors And Targeted Therapies
question: Which among the following is a hedgehog pathway inhibitor?

explanationHtml:
Venetoclax is a type of small-molecule inhibitor of B-cell lymphoma (BCL)2 that is approved for use in CLL with a 17p deletion.

Overexpression of BCL-2 has been demonstrated in CLL. Venetoclax displaces the proapoptotic proteins like BIM, triggering mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization and the activation of caspases, ultimately helping in the restoration of apoptosis by binding to the BCL-2 protein.

Other options:

Options A & B: Olaparib and rucaparib are inhibitors of PARP [Poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase] enzymes.

Option D: Vismodegib is a hedgehog pathway inhibitor.
lessonTitle: Interleukins, Growth Factors And Targeted Therapies
question: Evaluation of a patient with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) showed evidence of 17p deletion. Which of the following is a BCL-2 inhibitor approved for use in this condition?

explanationHtml:
Sipuleucel-T is a cell-based approach to induce an immune response against prostatic acid phosphatase (PAP) that is commonly expressed in prostatic cancer. It is approved for use in minimally symptomatic, hormone-refractory, metastatic prostate cancer.

Sipuleucel-T preparation is done by isolating a patient's peripheral blood cells by leukapheresis and then exposing them to PAP-GM-CSF (which is a human recombinant protein). When these treated cells are infused into the patient, the APCs present in the blood produce antibodies directed against PAP.

Prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) is a specific prostate epithelial cell membrane antigen, showing increased expression in prostate cancers, which is also a potential target for monoclonal antibody therapy.
lessonTitle: Interleukins, Growth Factors And Targeted Therapies
question: Sipuleucel-T is the first vaccine approved for the treatment of cancer. This vaccine induces an immune response against which of the following?

explanationHtml:
Febuxostat is a uric acid synthesis inhibitor that acts by inhibiting the enzyme xanthine oxidase and it is indicated in gout management.

Histone deacetylases (HDACs) are enzymes that promote gene silencing. In many cancers, HDACs are overactive, leading to the silencing of important tumor suppressor genes. HDAC inhibitors allow tumor suppressor genes to be expressed again, thereby reducing cancer growth. Examples of histone deacetylase inhibitors and their uses are:

  • Vorinostat - used in cutaneous T cell lymphoma
  • Belinostat - used in peripheral T cell lymphoma
  • Romidepsin - used in cutaneousT cell lymphoma
  • Panobinostat - used in multiple myeloma
lessonTitle: Interleukins, Growth Factors And Targeted Therapies
question: Which of the following is not a histone deacetylase inhibitor?

explanationHtml:
The scenario is suggestive of metastatic melanoma, and trametinib is used in this condition. It is a reversible inhibitor of the mitogen-activated extracellular signal-regulated kinase (MEK). It inhibits the serine-threonine kinase domain of the BRAF V600E mutant of MEK.

It can be used as a single agent, but it is more effective when used with BRAF inhibitors like dabrafenib. Other drugs in the class of MEK inhibitors are cobimetinib, binimetinib, and selumetinib.

Other options:

Options A and B: Dabrafenib and vemurafenib are BRAF inhibitors used in metastatic melanoma.

Option D: Ipilimumab is a human cytotoxic T-lymphocyte antigen 4 (CTLA-4) blocking antibody used in metastatic or unresectable melanoma.
lessonTitle: Interleukins, Growth Factors And Targeted Therapies
question: A 60-year-old woman was diagnosed with melanoma. Sentinel lymph node biopsy showed malignant cells. Which of the following drugs used in this condition is a MEK inhibitor?

explanationHtml:
Tisagenlecleucel is the first gene therapy-based treatment that is approved for use in acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL).

This therapy genetically modifies a patient's T cells, enabling them to express a Chimeric Antigen Receptor (CAR). This CAR specifically recognizes CD19 on leukemia cells, which in turn activates the modified T cells. Once activated, these T cells multiply and effectively eliminate cancer cells.
lessonTitle: Interleukins, Growth Factors And Targeted Therapies
question: A 4-year-old child who was being evaluated for pancytopenia is diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia. Which of the following is the first gene therapy-based treatment approved for use in this condition?

explanationHtml:
The clinical scenario points towards a diagnosis of metastatic ovarian cancer. Rucaparib is a poly ADP-ribose polymerase/ PARP inhibitor approved for the treatment of advanced ovarian cancer with BRCA mutations.

PARP is a nuclear protein that transfers ADP-ribose from NAD+ to target proteins, and this plays an important role in the DNA damage response. By inhibiting PARP, these drugs shut down the DNA repair pathway, leading to an accumulation of DNA damage that the cancer cells cannot fix, leading to their apoptosis. Rucaparib and olaparib are PARP inhibitors.

Other options:

Option A: Palbociclib is a selective inhibitor of the cyclin-dependent kinases CDK4 and CDK6. It is used in the treatment of metastatic breast cancer.

Options C & D: Vorinostat and romidepsin are histone deacetylase inhibitors.
lessonTitle: Interleukins, Growth Factors And Targeted Therapies
question: A 63-year-old postmenopausal woman came to the OPD with a 12 cm adnexal mass. Her CA-125 levels were raised and her risk of malignancy index was calculated to be 250. PET scan revealed hepatic metastases. Which PARP inhibitor can you use in her treatment?

explanationHtml:
A topical solution of hydrogen peroxide has been approved for the treatment of raised seborrheic keratoses.

Hydrogen peroxide is a keratolytic agent. Its exact mechanism of action in the treatment of seborrheic keratoses is not fully understood. Supraphysiologic concentrations may cause oxidative damage and death to seborrheic keratosis cells. Hydrogen peroxide is also commonly used as a disinfectant to clean wounds. It can also be used as a mouthwash.

Other treatment options for seborrheic keratoses are liquid nitrogen cryotherapy (first-line), electrodesiccation and curettage, ablative laser treatment, and shave biopsy.
lessonTitle: Interleukins, Growth Factors And Targeted Therapies
question: Which of the following conditions has hydrogen peroxide been recently approved for?

explanationHtml:
Apalutamide is an androgen receptor inhibitor indicated for the treatment of patients with non-metastatic castration-resistant and metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer.

Prostate cancer relies on androgens to grow, as these hormones activate the androgen receptor in cancer cells, driving their proliferation. Apalutamide works by binding directly to this receptor, preventing the action of androgen and blocking cancer cell growth. Other drugs with the same mechanism are enzalutamide and darolutamide.
lessonTitle: Interleukins, Growth Factors And Targeted Therapies
question: Which of the following conditions is apalutamide approved for?

explanationHtml:
The clinical scenario is suggestive of metastatic melanoma. The recombinant interleukin-2 (IL-2) preparation that is approved for use in metastatic melanoma is aldesleukin. It acts as an IL-2 agonist and is also approved for use in metastatic renal cell cancer.

Interleukin-2 stimulates the proliferation of activated T cells and the secretion of cytokines from NK cells and monocytes. IL-2 stimulation increases cytotoxic killing of cancer cells by T cells and NK cells.

Other options:

Option A: Denileukin diftitox is an immunotoxin made from the recombinant combination of IL-2 and the catalytically active fragment of diphtheria toxin. It is approved for use in cutaneous T cell lymphoma.

Options C & D: Imatinib and nilotinib are BCR/ABL tyrosine kinase inhibitors.
lessonTitle: Interleukins, Growth Factors And Targeted Therapies
question: A 60-year-old woman was diagnosed with melanoma. Sentinel lymph node biopsy showed malignant cells.  Which among the following is a recombinant interleukin-2 preparation approved for use in this condition?

correctAnswer: B. Fusion protein of IL-2 and diptheria toxin
explanationHtml:
Denileukin diftitox is an immunotoxin made from the genetic recombination of IL-2 and the catalytically active fragment of diphtheria toxin.

It is indicated for relapsed or refractory cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. After binding to the IL-2 receptors on cancer cells, it is internalized by endocytosis. The active fragment of diphtheria toxin is then released into the cytosol, where it inhibits protein synthesis through ADP ribosylation, leading to cell death.

Immunotoxins use a targeting protein(IL-2 in this case) coupled to a toxin.

Antibody-drug conjugates are complex molecules composed of an antibody linked to an anticancer drug. These conjugates are cell-specific to kill efficiently the target cells. Examples are:

  • Gemtuzumab ozogamicin - Monoclonal antibody against CD33 linked to a semisynthetic derivative of calicheamicin, a potent antitumor antibiotic. It was approved for the treatment of acute myeloid leukemia.
  • Brentuximab vedotin - Used for the treatment of Hodgkin's and anaplastic lymphoma, it is an anti-CD30 IgG1 monoclonal antibody linked with the microtubule-disrupting agent MMAE.
  • Ado-trastuzumab emtansine - It combines the HER2-targeted properties of trastuzumab with the antimicrotubule agent DM1 (derived from maytansine), allowing preferential intracellular drug delivery to HER2+ cells. It is used in the treatment of HER+ breast cancer.
